summary:
I've written plan.md: a long, low single-storey house of white stucco and dark timber under a pale slab roof that rises only 1.5 blocks over a 10-cell half-span. Its eaves are 2 deep, beam ends stick out past them every 3 cells, and a flat carport roof sits one level lower beside it. The street side is blank apart from a tan ledgestone wall, a clerestory strip and an orange door; the back is floor-to-ceiling glass between dark posts, opening onto a kidney pool. Those layered horizontals, the central atrium and the teal-and-white car on the driveway are what make it read as an Eichler or Palm Springs house. Long white-stucco, dark-timber post-and-beam bungalow: stepped-slab near-flat gable on beam lines every 3, flat carport deck one level lower, blank street face with ledgestone wall and orange door, all-glass garden side, open-sky atrium at the centre.
Open-plan public core (gallery, galley kitchen, dining, living with sunken pit and freestanding fireplace) west of the atrium; corridor with 3 bedrooms and 2 baths east.
Teal/white car, desert front yard, kidney pool and patio behind. 6 parts; elements.md and the plan.md designer sections are written.

house shell and ground: parts/shell.mjs builds the house shell and ground: bedding, floor slab (terrazzo, spruce, quartz, with air over pit, atrium and chimney), perimeter base, stucco body and header, door wall, atrium ring body and header, partitions with doorways, and the y=5 spruce ceiling.
Every opening the later parts need is left as air. make.sh completes; the shell line shows 1840 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE, and the check reports walkable end to end.
Render tiles read as a low white box with openings and header bands; the south glazing and corner posts are left for part 4.
polish: Corner posts (10/31, z=8 and z=25) and the south wall glass/posts are left as air for part 4; part 4 must place them.
Atrium ring body (x=16/22 and z=11/18, y=2..4) and ring corner posts are air for part 4 glass and posts.
Clerestory cells (x=22..30, y=4, z=8) are air for part 4 glazing and mullions.
Ceiling and header cells at y=5 over the south and atrium rows float until part 4 glazes the walls and part 3 lays the beam logs (check reports 30 floating blocks, all of which resolve then).
elements 13 (slider gaps) and 16 (atrium ring) are only partly built: the gaps and ring body are air as specified, the glazing is part 4's.

waste.what: Worked out each opening, partition and doorway cell by cell in code (the openBox predicate list and the per-room floor rectangles) from plan.md OPENINGS and ROOMS.
waste.cost: about 25 openBox/rect calls hand-derived; several coordinate mistakes caught only by reading the spec again
waste.tool: a helper that takes the plan.md OPENINGS table (or rooms.json) and returns air cells to keep, plus a per-room floor-material lookup from ROOMS, so the perimeter and partition loops are not written by hand

waste.what: Perimeter stucco and base loops, skipping openings, were written as local per-cell loops instead of stucco_wall.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of loop code; stucco_wall cannot skip openings, so it was not used for the walls
waste.tool: stucco_wall with an optional openings list (cells to leave air), or a wall_run(x0,z0,x1,z1,y0,y1,{openings}) helper

waste.what: Partitions with doorways (y=2..3 air, y=4 lintel) written as a local helper.
waste.cost: one local helper plus 6 calls
waste.tool: a partition(line, doors) vocab helper that matches plan.md ROOMS partitions and doorway cells

summary:
site, carport and paving: parts/site.mjs builds the sidewalk, driveway with four joint rows, sand front yard with gravel beds and cactus-root sand, stepping pads and landing, carport (deck, posts, beams, fascia, floor) with its breeze-block screen, back patio, pool deck (pool cells left empty) and back lawns.
make.sh runs whole: site part placed 933, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd render and the front-left tile show the driveway, carport deck, sand yard and pool deck where plan.md puts them.
Ticked plan.md part 2 and elements 5, 6, 11, 18, 19, 25 in elements.md; element 24 is left open for the paving-only part, with a note in plan.md Notes.
polish: Element 24 (back patio and pool deck): paving is built, but the lounger and patio-table furniture and the palm at (29,31) belong to part 6, so the item stays unticked.
Breeze-block screen ends at (1,3,21) and (9,3,21) are flagged as orphans by `mcd check`. This is intended for a pierced screen, not a fault.
Front-yard cacti sit on the sand I laid under their five trunk cells, but the cacti themselves and the palms come from part 5 (front.mjs); nothing of theirs is placed here.
The floating-block and enclosed-cell warnings in `mcd check` come from the shell and roof parts (floor and ceiling at y=5), not from this part.

waste.what: Worked out the ground-cover split by hand (sand vs grass vs carport floor at x=0/x=9, z=22..25), and checked cell lists for the cactus-root sand, cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 6 minutes of reasoning and several rewrites of the ground() calls; one ordering bug (a grass fill overwrote the x=9 sand strip) found only after reading my own code.
waste.tool: A ground-cover spec as data in plan.md (rect, block, order) that a builder can iterate, so the split is decided once in the plan rather than by each worker in code.

waste.what: Ticking the checklists: Edit needs a Read of plan.md and elements.md first, which the shared kit says not to do, so I used perl -pi for the ticks.
waste.cost: two failed sed attempts and one perl pass.
waste.tool: A `mcd tick <file> <item-id>` command (or plan.md checklist ids) that marks an element done without a Read/Edit round trip.

waste.what: Reading the stub of each vocab helper to learn whether it writes over dirt at y=0 (every helper writes only into air, and build.mjs lays dirt on the whole lot at y=0).
waste.cost: one grep of vocab/h3.mjs and the place() helper; the other helpers' over-behaviour was inferred from their comments.
waste.tool: A note in the kit saying y=0 is dirt before runParts, and which helpers accept an over option for ground cover (stepping_pad does, most do not).

summary:
roofs, beams and fireplace stack: parts/roofs.mjs builds the stepped slab roof (4 bands, ridge along x, dark_oak_slab fascia round the outer ring and both holes), beam_line on x=10..31, gable-end and atrium-ring glass at y=6, and the fireplace stack at x=20..21 z=21..22 (y=1..8).
make.sh gives 738 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows 0 floating; the front-left and back elevation tiles read as a low stepped roof with dark fascia, beam ends and the flue in the atrium-side hole.
Ticked elements 2, 3, 14 in elements.md and "3 roofs" in plan.md; added a Notes line.

waste.what: Worked out the band table by hand: which z rows and y for bands A, B, C and the ridge, and which top/bottom half each takes, from plan.md ROOFS.
waste.cost: about 8 rows of coordinates read off the spec and typed into roof_band calls; one pass, no retries
waste.tool: a roof_stack(g, {bands:[[zA,zB,y,half]...], fascia, holes}) helper in vocab, or a plan.md machine-readable band table, would have made this one call.

waste.what: Checked by eye which beam-line cells were the designed exposed tails versus real problems in mcd check output.
waste.cost: 16 ORPHAN warnings on the z=5 and z=28 beam ends, verified by reading the plan rather than fixing
waste.tool: mcd check could take a beam-tail allowance (or the plan's exposed-tail list) so intentional overhangs are not reported as orphans.

summary:
facades, glazing and entry: parts/facades.mjs builds the south garden glass wall (posts on every beam line, glass between them, three sliders with y=4 glass), the atrium ring glazing and posts, the gable-end and side windows, the utility door, the north clerestory, the orange entry and the ledgestone wall with cap.
make.sh runs whole: facades placed 226, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; mcd check shows only the expected floating y=6 glass (the roof part supplies its support) and the street and back elevations read as the concept.
Ticked plan.md checklist item 4 and elements.md items 4, 8-10, 12-16; the gable-end and ring y=6 glass is also named by part 3, so the two parts overlap there.
polish: Gable-end glass (x=10 and x=31, y=6, z=14..19) and ring glass at y=6 (x=16 and x=22, z=14..17) are also in part 3's spec. Both parts write identical blocks, so the first merged write wins and the other is refused as a duplicate; the merge should drop one.
mcd check shows FLOATING glass at y=6 in this run only because the roof part is still a stub; the roof part should clear it.
The dark_oak_door utility door is written with explicit states (open=true, powered=false), not through a vocab helper; no helper was checked against the plan beyond the render.

waste.what: Worked out the glass segments between the south-wall posts by hand, interleaving the three slider gaps (x=14..15, 20..21, 26..27) so no glass landed in the y=2..3 door air.
waste.cost: about 8 glass_bay calls and the slider bookkeeping, worked out cell by cell
waste.tool: A helper that fills the spans between beam-line posts on a wall run and skips listed gap x-ranges, e.g. bay_run(g, z, x0, x1, y0, y1, {gaps:[...]}).

waste.what: Wrote the atrium ring glass, the lintel posts and the door-side glass as separate glass_bay calls per side, with the y=4 glass above the doors split out by hand.
waste.cost: about 12 calls, with the door-column exceptions worked out per cell
waste.tool: A ring-builder helper for the atrium (glass sides, corner posts, door cells with lintel), or a glass_bay option that skips a cell range.

waste.what: Wrote the utility door's lower and upper halves with explicit states, since B.door has no open option and the helper set has no plain door helper.
waste.cost: one local helper, about 10 lines
waste.tool: B.door with an open option, or a door helper in vocab h4 that writes both halves with open=true and powered=false.

waste.what: Checked the look by reading the street and back-elevation tiles, and judged the posts and sliders against the plan by eye.
waste.cost: 2 image reads, no numeric comparison
waste.tool: mcd check or a tile-level diff against the plan's opening table (cells expected glass, post, door, air) that prints mismatches.

summary:
car and front garden: Part 5 (car and front garden) is built in parts/front.mjs: the teal two-tone 1950s car at x=3..5 z=1..7, palms at (12,3) and (30,4), a saguaro pair and barrel cacti in the x=23..29 z=2..4 bed, four dead bushes on the front sand, and the mailbox at (9,1). make.sh gives a whole build.nbt: the front part places 105 blocks, with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. Renders read correctly: the car, cacti, palms and mailbox sit where plan.md puts them.</summary>
<parameter name="waste">[{"what":"Dead bushes placed one by one with a hand-written loop of g.set calls on chosen sand cells, and the cells picked by hand against the gravel beds, cacti, pads and landing.","cost":"4 cells, about 3 minutes of coordinate checking against plan.md","tool":"A scatter helper in vocab (e.g. scatter(g, box, block, {exclude: [...], count, seed}) that only writes into air on sand at y=1) would have replaced the hand list."},{"what":"Checked the placed cells by reading the 'car and front garden' line of parts-report.json with a one-off node command, then re-ran mcd check to see which flags were from my part.","cost":"2 extra tool calls","tool":"make.sh could print only the line for the part being built (or mcd check could take --part to filter its output)."}]
polish: Cacti conflict with the site part: plan.md's site spec puts gravel beds on x=22..30 z=1..5, but the cactus cluster and elements item 21 say sand under each cactus. My cacti stand at y=1..3 and write nothing at y=0, so the site part must decide the y=0 cell (sand is what cacti need to survive). Needs a reading from the site worker or the architect.

mcd check flags the palm crown leaves as ORPHAN jungle_leaves (sticks out sideways, touches the build on one face). They are persistent leaves held by the trunk, so this is expected, not a fault; the roofs part puts the roof over palm (30,4)'s crown at z=6 and the palm helper skips roof cells, which is fine since roofs runs before front.
Dead bushes are placed with a direct g.set call (not a vocab helper); fine as-is, but a scatter helper would be the tidy form.

summary: pool, patio and garden details: Back garden built in parts/back.mjs: pool water in the reserved cells, three loungers and a patio table on the patio, a palm at (29,31), four garden lamps, and seeded short grass on the lawns. make.sh exits 0 with a whole build.nbt; this part's line shows 83 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
polish: Pool coping not laid: the rim is site's locked smooth_stone deck, so the coping would be refused at merge. Site should lay the rim as smooth_quartz_slab (bottom) at y=0; cell list in plan.md Notes.
Pool liner and floor (y=-2..-1) are below the grid and dropped; only the y=0 water is in build.nbt.
Elements 23 and 24 not ticked (23 lacks coping and liner; 24 needs site's paving). 26 is ticked, and plan checklist item 6 is ticked.
Short grass is placed only on grass_block at y=0; site is still a stub in this run, so the count is 0 here and needs a re-check after the merge.
Palm (29,31) crown leaves flagged as orphans by mcd check: a crown-shape quirk of the palm helper, not a placement error.

waste.what: Worked out the pool rim cells by hand to explain what the coping needs from the site part.
waste.cost: about 20 cells, one reasoning pass
waste.tool: A kidney_pool option { coping: false } or a mcd pool-rim command that lists the rim without writing.

waste.what: Hand-wrote a seeded scatter loop for short_grass over the 34x34 footprint, with a grass_block check per cell.
waste.cost: one 20-line loop, 0 retries
waste.tool: A scatter(g, box, block, {over, density, seed}) brush in the build library.

waste.what: Rewrote back.mjs once because kidney_pool() also writes coping into the locked deck, so the pool was redone as a local water-only helper.
waste.cost: one rewrite plus one failed sed edit
waste.tool: A split pool_water() vs coping() in vocab/h1.mjs, so a part can skip cells an earlier part owns.

summary: room: gallery: Gallery (room 1) built as three hung lanterns at (17|19|21, y=4, z=10). Room check: walk OK (7/7 cells reachable), light min 11, no dark cells. make.sh saves a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines for this part.
polish: Low birch bench not built: every cell of the one-deep strip (x=16..22, z=10) is on a required 2-high route, so no bench fits on the floor without blocking the kitchen, corridor, front-door or atrium paths. Needs a decision from the architect (for example a bench on the north wall outside the box, or accepting a walkable low slab).
Item-frame art on the north wall not built: item frames are entities, not blocks, and the north wall cells (z=9) are outside the gallery box.

Lantern at (19,4,10) is refused in a local build because the roof part's beam at (19,5,10) is not yet there; it should place in the merged build (roofs part runs before rooms). Confirm in the merged build that it reports 3 lanterns.

plan.md Notes gained a line for part 7 describing the constraint. elements.md item 30 (entry gallery with bench and coat hooks) is NOT ticked because the bench and art are missing; item 35 (lit) is covered for this room only.

waste.what: Worked out by hand that the gallery box is one cell deep and every cell is a route to a door or opening, so no floor furniture fits; checked the floor grid and walk verdict by reasoning rather than a tool that flags route-critical cells
waste.cost: about 4 minutes of analysis; no blocks wasted
waste.tool: mcd plan could mark cells on a required route (front door to each opening) as 'route', so a room this narrow reports up front that nothing can stand on the floor

waste.what: hung_lantern placement depends on the roof part's beam at (19,5,10); in a local build without the roofs part the lantern at x=19 was silently refused and I only learned it from the census (2 lanterns, not 3)
waste.cost: one build-and-check cycle
waste.tool: hung_lantern could return a placed/refused flag, or the room check could list refused writes per part, so a missing support is visible without reading the census

summary:
room: kitchen: Kitchen interior built in parts/room-2.mjs: galley counter on the north wall (furnace hob, cauldron sink, iron fridge, spruce trapdoor cabinets, potted cactus, flower pot), a spruce-fence and slab breakfast bar on z=12 with a walk-through gap at x=13 and birch-slab stools on z=13, an orange carpet runner, and one hanging lantern at (13,4,11).
Room check: walk OK (16/16 reachable), light min 10, no dark cells; make.sh gives 27 kitchen placements with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE. Ticked elements.md item 29.
Whole build.nbt produced; the part reads as a galley kitchen with bar in the room render.
polish: The lantern at (13,4,11) hangs from the ceiling beam at (13,5,11), which part 3 (roofs, beam_line x=13) lays; until then `mcd check` reports it UNSUPPORTED. Nothing for this part to fix.
The render was checked from above and inside; the kitchen reads correctly. The whole-house render was not checked, because the other parts are still stubs.
Lighting depends on the lantern alone (min light 10 at the feet); if the roof part changes the ceiling, recheck the room.

waste.what: Worked out the kitchen furniture cell by cell and wrote it as four text layers by hand, then fixed the bar legs after a check reported orphan slabs.
waste.cost: about 3 build-check cycles; the first layout had orphan bar slabs and a bar that blocked the walk-through.
waste.tool: A galley-with-bar helper that takes a gap position and fits the legs under every top slab; or `mcd plan` output with a rule like 'every slab needs a support below'.

waste.what: Checked by eye whether the bar gap and the stools leave a walkable route from the dining opening, because galley_kitchen puts the bar on every other cell with no gap.
waste.cost: one reasoning pass over the walk; the room check confirmed it afterwards.
waste.tool: galley_kitchen could take an optional gap column for the walk-through, or a `mcd room` run that suggests bar gaps.

waste.what: Checked whether a hanging lantern is supported by a beam that another part lays, because the room check can't see parts that aren't built yet.
waste.cost: one `mcd check` read and a note in left.
waste.tool: A per-part `check` that resolves supports from the full plan (for example by running the roofs part in the same build), not only the parts built so far.

summary:
room: dining: Dining room (parts/room-3.mjs) is built inside its box x 11..15, y 2..4, z 14..18: a spruce-top table on spruce fence legs with three birch chairs on each long side, a birch sideboard with a potted cactus under the west window, spruce panelling on the west wall at z=17..18, and two hung lanterns from the x=13 beam (the pendant over the table is the focal light).
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt; the dining line reads placed 32, refused 0, offPalette []. `mcd room --only dining` says OK: 19 of 19 floor cells reachable, min light 10, 0 dark. elements.md item 28 is ticked.
Problems: the lanterns hang from the beam at x=13, which the roofs part (still a stub here) must provide; until then `mcd check` reports them UNSUPPORTED. The room check is clean now because the room check doesn't look at beams.
polish: The pendant lanterns at (13,4,15) and (13,4,17) hang from the beam line x=13 at y=5, which the roofs part must build. In this session roofs is a stub, so `mcd check` flags both lanterns as UNSUPPORTED; they should be supported once the roofs part is merged.
The floor is the shell's terrazzo at y=1; the dining part does not lay its own floor.

Wall panelling is on the west wall only, at x=11 z=17..18 (spruce trapdoors, open, against x=10), because the other sides of the room are openings or glass (north to the kitchen, south to the living room, east to the atrium ring).
The dining_set helper was not used: its footprint (chairs at x-1 and x+2 along z) collides with the west sideboard in a 5-wide room, so the table runs along x instead (x 12..14, z 15..16).
plan.md's checklist has no room-level ticks; only elements.md item 28 is ticked. Items 33 (panelling/terrazzo) and 35 (every room lit) are not ticked because they span other rooms.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture cell by hand on a 5x5 floor: table orientation, chair facings, which cells the sideboard, panels and lanterns take, and checking that the north and south lanes stay open.
waste.cost: about 40 cells placed through layers() with hand-computed coordinates, plus one redesign after finding that dining_set's chair footprint clashes with the sideboard
waste.tool: A room-fitting helper: `dining_set` (or a `table_for(n)` helper) that takes the room box and the wall the sideboard sits on, then picks the table axis and chair rows that keep the entry lanes clear. Or `mcd plan --suggest` returning a furniture layout for the floor grid.

waste.what: Looked up the layers() legend state format and the B.* helper signatures by reading the build library source.
waste.cost: one grep and one source read, about 2 minutes
waste.tool: A short reference card in the kit listing each B.* helper's output state keys (for example trapdoor open is a string 'true'/'false') and the layers() legend format.

waste.what: Checked whether the lanterns were supported and whether the room was lit by running `mcd check` and `mcd room` on a build where the roofs part was still a stub.
waste.cost: two toolkit runs; the check flagged both lanterns, which only the roofs part can fix
waste.tool: `mcd room --rooms` could take a per-room 'needs' list (for example a beam at y=5 over x=13 for z=14..18) so cross-part dependencies show as a named wait, not a generic UNSUPPORTED.

waste.what: Rendered the whole house to see the interior part, although the room sits inside walls and only `mcd rooms --only dining` shows it.
waste.cost: one full render (about 10 s) that could not show the part
waste.tool: Skip the whole-house render for interior-only parts, or add a `--room` mode to `mcd render` that cuts the house down to one room box.

summary:
room: living: Living room built in parts/room-4.mjs: sunken conversation pit with orange rim cushions and table, two orange sofas (west, east) plus an orange egg chair by the atrium glass, a birch sideboard on the north edge, spruce panelling on the x=21 side of the x=22 partition, a dark-oak-and-end-rod floor lamp in the SW corner, and three hung lanterns.
make.sh finishes with a whole build.nbt; room-4 placed 61 blocks with 0 refused and 0 off-palette. mcd room says OK: 51 of 52 floor cells reachable (the one unreached cell is the sideboard's potted cactus top), 0 dark cells, min light 6.
Ticked elements.md item 27 only; the fireplace it names is the roof part's.
polish: Freestanding fireplace (x=20..21, z=21..22) is the roof part's; room-4 leaves those cells alone, and the campfire focus only appears once parts/roofs.mjs runs.
Tulip side table (elements 34) not built.
Floor lamp is a fence and end_rod placed by hand, not a vocab helper.
The pit's inner floor is y=0 from the shell; the rim stairs are at y=1 so their tops sit at the living floor height.
Second sofa's arms run into the sideboard's neighbourhood only at z=21 and z=24, which are clear; no conflict found.
Hung lanterns: none at z=19 (vault open above the lane), so the atrium lane is lit by the lantern at (20,4,20).
Elements 33 (terrazzo, panelling) and 35 (every room lit) are only partly met by this room and are left unticked.
Structure check shows floating groups for the ceiling and headers because the roof and beams parts are still stubs in this copy; not from room-4.

waste.what: Worked out each furniture footprint and its walking clearance by hand from the plan's floor grid, then tried positions by trial and error: the first egg chair and sideboard placements cut the walk, and a hung lantern at z=19 was refused because the vault above that row is open.
waste.cost: about 4 build/check cycles, roughly 6 coordinate choices re-derived by hand
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --place` mode or a helper that lists free footprints for a given furniture size and clearance (e.g. 2x4 sofa with arms, egg chair 3x3) and reports which ceiling cells have a block above (hang-able) before placing.

waste.what: Panelling for the x=22 partition is one panel_wall call per z row, and the sideboard, sofa and pit had to be checked one by one against the walk report.
waste.cost: 2 extra calls and one re-run of make.sh
waste.tool: panel_wall accepting a z range (or a box), and a dry-run flag on the vocab helpers that returns the cells they would fill without writing.

summary:
room: atrium: parts/room-5.mjs now furnishes the atrium with layers(): smooth_stone stepping pads at y=1 on the x=19..20 path, a grass and fern patch, a small jungle sapling (focal) on the west side, a birch_stairs bench and potted cacti on the east, and hung lanterns on the x=19 beam plus standing lanterns (41 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette).
The room check passes: walk OK (29 of 29 cells reachable), min light 10 at the feet, 0 dark cells. make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the rooms render was read and looks right.
Ticked elements.md item 17 and added an atrium note to plan.md Notes.
polish: Hung lanterns at (19,4,13) and (19,4,17) hang from the x=19 beam at y=5, which the roofs part (still a stub in this session) must place; `mcd check` reports them unsupported until the merged build has it.
Grass is short_grass on the shell's dirt, not grass_block (y=0 is locked to the shell); the potted palm and rocks from the spec were not built.
The street and front tiles don't show the atrium (it sits under the roof), so the only look was the room render.

waste.what: Worked the atrium's floor layout by hand, one y-layer at a time, to keep the 2-wide walk clear and the lanterns on the x=19 beam
waste.cost: one design pass over 4 layers of 5x6 cells, then two fixes after the first walk/light check

waste.cost: about 10 coordinate checks; the hung lanterns report UNSUPPORTED in check because the roofs part is still a stub

summary:
room: corridor: Corridor interior built in parts/room-6.mjs with layers(): a clear 1-wide walking lane at x=23 from z=9 to 21, and a x=24 furniture column with a birch sideboard and potted cactus (z=11..13), a bookshelf focal wall (z=16..18), potted plants (z=9, z=20) and four lanterns (three hung from the spruce ceiling, one standing on the bookshelf).
mcd room reports OK: every floor cell reachable, minimum light 10 at the feet, 0 dark cells. make.sh wrote a whole build.nbt; the corridor line shows 19 placed, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks.
Item-frame art and the terrazzo floor are not built here; a bed or wardrobe would need the bedroom parts. The render shows the sideboard and bookshelf reading clearly from above.
polish: No item-frame art: item frames are entities, not blocks, so the brief's art is absent (plan.md Notes should say so).
Terrazzo floor is the shell's at y=1; the corridor part adds nothing there.

Elements 31 (bedrooms' beds and wardrobes) and 35 (every room lit) are not ticked: 31 needs the bedroom parts, 35 is whole-house. The plan.md checklist only lists parts 1-6, so there was no room tick to make.
Two y=4 cells on top of the bookshelf (24,4,16) and (24,4,18) are free but unreachable; mcd room lists them as WALK-unreached but still says OK. Cosmetic.

waste.what: Wrote the layers() rows as 3-character strings with a space separator (". P"), so every furniture char landed on x=25 and the part was refused 19 times. Found it only from the parts report after a make.sh run.
waste.cost: One full make.sh round and one report read; about 19 refused writes.
waste.tool: A layers() row-width check: it should fail when a row's length differs from the room's floor width, and print the origin's x range, so the 'x mod' column mismatch is caught before the build.

summary:
room: bedroom 1: Bedroom 1 (guest/child, blue-teal) is built in parts/room-7.mjs: light-blue double bed on the centre column with a 2-high spruce headboard on the north wall, spruce-fence nightstands with birch-slab tops, a 1-wide spruce wardrobe with open trapdoor fronts on the east end of the north wall, a bookshelf with a flower pot in the north-west corner, a cyan carpet at the foot, and two hung lanterns.
make.sh gives a whole build.nbt. The part places 20 blocks with no refused writes and no off-palette blocks; room check says OK, 15 of 15 floor cells reachable, min light 10, no dark cells. The room render reads as a bedroom with the bed as the focal piece.
Used the layers() text grid for the furniture and hung_lantern for the two lanterns. The walk check caught a dead corner cell (27,9), which I fixed by moving the bookshelf west.
polish: plan.md checklist and elements.md item 31 (three bedrooms, beds, wardrobes, nightstands) and item 35 (every room lit) are NOT ticked: this part covers bedroom 1 only, so the tick belongs to the whole-house pass once bedroom 2 and the master exist.

The headboard is a 2-high spruce_planks run at (28,2..3,9) against the north wall rather than a bed_double call, because the helper's footprint does not fit this 5x4 room; the bed itself is a hand-placed light_blue_bed pair with facing north (foot at 28,11; head at 28,10).
The window on the east wall (x=31, z=10..12) and the doorway (25,10) are untouched; the wardrobe sits at x=30, z=9, clear of the window at z=10..12 and of the door lane.
Nothing is over the doorway or window: the hung lanterns are at (27,4,11) and (30,4,11) and the flower pot at (27,4,9).

waste.what: Worked out the 5x4 furniture grid cell by cell by hand, then checked it by re-running make.sh and mcd room after each move.
waste.cost: about 3 rebuild cycles, one dead corner cell (27,9) found only by the walk check and fixed by moving the bookshelf
waste.tool: mcd plan should print the floor with a candidate furniture grid and report unreachable cells before any build, and bed_double should accept a headboard footprint that fits a narrow room.

waste.what: My first attempt to edit the module used a python heredoc that held node code, so the edit silently did nothing and I had to redo it with the edit tool.
waste.cost: one wasted shell call
waste.tool: the edit tool directly; no shell rewrites of the part source.

summary:
room: bath 1: Bath 1 built: bath_fit at x=26..27, z=14..16 (cauldron basin with glass mirror, quartz-stair WC, two quartz-slab tub cells at z=16) with the z=15 row kept clear as the lane from the doorway, plus a sea_lantern on top of the mirror at (26,4,14).
make.sh finished with a whole build.nbt; the bath 1 line shows 6 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE.
`mcd room --only "bath 1"` says OK: 5 of 5 floor cells reachable, min light 11, 0 dark cells.
polish: plan.md has no checklist line for room parts, so nothing ticked there; elements.md item 32 'Two bathrooms' is only half done (bath 1 built, bath 2 is part 15).

The WC's stair facing comes from bath_fit (facing south). The toolkit says stairs' facing is the side of the full-height back, which would put the back on the south and the seat toward the wall. That contradicts the usual vanilla reading. Needs a close look in the final render; I did not check the in-game orientation.

The rooms render gave only the from-above view; the room is 2x3 so no inside eye view was produced. I did not look at a full-house render tile for this part (it is an interior, not visible from outside).
check reports 30 floating blocks at y=5 over x=14..21 z=18..25 (spruce_planks, dark_oak_planks). These come from the ceiling and header rows of other parts that are still stubs; none are from bath 1.

waste.what: Fixture layout worked out by hand: I read the plan grid and picked bath_fit's offset by hand so the 2x3 footprint matched the room and the lane stayed clear.
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of reading helper source and the plan grid; no retries
waste.tool: a `mcd plan --fit <helper>` or a room-fit check that takes a vocab helper name and reports whether its footprint fits the room box and which lane cells stay free

waste.what: The room check and the rooms render give only a from-above view for a tiny room; an inside eye view was not produced for the 2x3 box.
waste.cost: one extra render call, no interior look
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --eye` (or an eye view auto-placed at the room's entrance) for rooms smaller than 5 cells wide

summary:
room: bath 2: Bath 2 (parts/room-9.mjs) is built: basin under a mirror, quartz-stairs WC against the north wall and a one-cell quartz tub on the south-east corner. A standing lantern over the WC lights it, and the entry cell (29,16) stays clear.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with 5 bath-2 blocks, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes. `mcd room --only "bath 2"` says OK: 6 of 6 cells reachable, min light 11, 0 dark.
I added a Notes line to plan.md: bath_fit's tub seals the doorway, so bath 2 does not use it.
polish: Shower: the spec allows tub or shower; I built a one-cell tub only, no shower.
elements.md item 32 (two bathrooms) is only half done; bath 1 belongs to another part, so the item is not ticked.
plan.md checklist not ticked: its six parts do not include room parts.
No full render of build.nbt (only the room check and rooms.png); the room is inside the house and was judged from the room picture.
No hung lantern: the vault over z=14..19 is open, so nothing hangs from a ceiling; the lantern stands on the WC instead.

waste.what: Chose bath_fit for the bath layout, then found its tub fills both south cells and seals the doorway landing (walk UNREACHABLE); rewrote the fixture by hand with five set() calls.
waste.cost: One failed make.sh + room check cycle and one rewrite; about 5 set() calls by hand.
waste.tool: bath_fit with an option for the tub footprint (one cell, or the far row only), or mcd room/plan suggesting a clear doorway landing before a helper is chosen.

waste.what: Checked the light by reading the room check's LIGHT LEVELS grid and moved the lantern by hand to put the basin in the brightest light.
waste.cost: Two build/check cycles.
waste.tool: mcd light with a suggested lantern cell that maximises the light on a named focal cell.

summary:
room: bedroom 2: Bedroom 2 is built in parts/room-10.mjs as one layers() call over 3 height layers: yellow bed against the east wall (foot x29, head x30), nightstands, wardrobe on the north wall, desk with a stair-seat chair in the SW corner, yellow carpet runner, hung lantern under the x=28 beam, desk lamp, flower pot.
make.sh ran clean (18 placed, no REFUSED, no off-palette). `mcd room` says OK: 12/12 floor cells reachable, min light 11, no dark cells. The from-above view reads as a yellow bedroom.
The two doorways (corridor at x=25 z=19, bath 2 at x=29 z=17) connect through a free lane across the room.
polish: The hung lantern at (28,4,19) hangs from the beam_line(28) cell at (28,5,19), which the roofs part (parts/roofs.mjs) builds. Until that merges, `mcd check` flags it as UNSUPPORTED. Not a problem in my part, but it has to be checked after the merge.
Not ticked in elements.md: item 31 covers all three bedrooms and item 35 covers every room, so bedroom 2 alone cannot tick them. plan.md's checklist has no room rows.
No full-house render was run: the other parts are still stubs, so the room view (room.png) was the check I used.
No plan.md Notes line was added; nothing in the vocabulary was missing for this room.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture cell by cell in a 5x3 room to keep a walk lane from the corridor door (25,19) to the bath door (29,17), after bed_double's footprint split the room and cut off the bath side.
waste.cost: about 4 candidate layouts checked by hand, roughly 15 minutes of reasoning, and one wrong bed footprint (a bed across the west door lane) worked out and discarded
waste.tool: A `mcd plan`-driven helper that tries candidate furniture (bed_double with facing/offset, wardrobe, desk) against the room box and the entry cells, and reports the walk verdict before any write. Also a bed_double option to place the head on a wall, which fits small rooms.

waste.what: Confirmed the bed head-foot facing rule and the lantern/slab state strings by hand, with no check before writing.
waste.cost: one make.sh cycle and a read of the helper source
waste.tool: `mcd states yellow_bed` / `mcd states lantern` output in the kit header, or layers() accepting the same state names as the validated `mcd states` list

summary:
room: master bedroom: Master bedroom built in parts/room-11.mjs as one layers() drawing: wardrobe on the west wall, two orange beds with barrel nightstands (one lantern, one potted cactus), and an orange-upholstered egg-chair seat by the east glass. Hung lanterns under the ceiling at x=24, 27 and 30 plus the standing nightstand lantern.
`mcd room` says OK: 15 of 15 floor cells reachable, min light 11, no dark cells. make.sh finished with a whole build.nbt, 24 placed, no refused writes, no off-palette blocks; the render reads as a bedroom with orange beds and a wardrobe wall.
polish: plan.md has no room-11 tick line and elements.md items 31 (three bedrooms), 33 (floors/panelling) and 35 (every room lit) span several rooms, so I left them unticked for the coordinator to tick once all bedrooms are in.
The bed's headboard is the existing z=21 partition wall: there is no separate spruce headboard block above the beds.

The egg chair is a one-row custom build (orange stair seat at (30,2,23) facing the glass, iron-trapdoor back at x=29). The vocab egg_chair needs a 3x3 footprint that doesn't fit at x=31, so it has no arms.
The FLOATING warnings in `mcd check` (x=14..21, z=18..25, y=5) belong to other parts' ceiling and roof cells, not to this room; nothing in my part floats.

waste.what: Drew the room's furniture grid by hand: worked out each cell's character in three y-layers and the bed/stairs/trapdoor states, then re-checked the walk by eye.
waste.cost: about 3 layers x 3 rows of hand-typed characters; 2 full re-derivations of the bed orientation (head = foot + facing) and the stair facing for the egg chair
waste.tool: A `mcd plan --furnish` step that takes a per-room list of named furniture pieces (bed at x,z facing, nightstand, egg chair, wardrobe run) and writes the layers() rows, plus a bed/king helper that takes a two-wide bed footprint.

waste.what: The egg chair vocab helper needs a 3x3 footprint, which doesn't fit the glass-edge corner here, so I hand-wrote a one-row version.
waste.cost: one retry of the layout to find free cells for the seat and back
waste.tool: An egg_chair variant or a footprint option (back-only, against a wall or glass) in vocab h1, plus a `mcd plan` view that marks cells free for a given footprint.
